exposure: Rheumatic diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, ankylosing spondylitis, Sjogren's disease, sarcoidosis, undifferentiated connective tissue disease, other autoimmune conditions)
cohort: The study included 360 pregnancies in individuals diagnosed with various rheumatic diseases (RA, SLE, SSc, AS, Sjogren's disease, sarcoidosis, UCTD, and other autoimmune conditions) followed at Ankara University Faculty of Medicine.
finding: The study found an increased risk of preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, and neonatal complications in pregnancies complicated by rheumatic diseases, with specific hemogram-derived inflammatory markers predicting adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: RA patients experiencing disease flares had an 87.5% cesarean section rate, which significantly exceeded the general population rate.
